title: Binder Pools, Coroutines, Synchronisation, and Deadlocks Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies binder pools, coroutines, synchronisation, and deadlocks?
options: Keep locks away from remote or unknown calls, model actual dispatcher and Binder threads, and diagnose the complete wait-for graph.
questions.answer: Keep locks away from remote or unknown calls, model actual dispatcher and Binder threads, and diagnose the complete wait-for graph.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: A suspend function never blocks the thread that invokes it.
questions.explanation: Increasing a Binder or coroutine thread pool can hide saturation briefly while preserving the wait cycle that causes the failure.

questions.prompt: Why should state be copied before a synchronous Binder call?
questions.answer: It avoids holding an application lock across remote work that can block, reenter, call back, or die.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
